_meta.description: Ground truth for SentinelMesh Module A (Week 1). One entry per scenario: MITRE ATT&CK tactic/technique, CVE where applicable, target container, ordered attack path, severity (1-5), asset criticality (1-5), and the exact detection output each scenario must produce.
_meta.severity_scale: 1=informational, 2=low, 3=moderate, 4=high, 5=critical — independent of Falco/detector's own CRITICAL/WARNING label, which is a detection-priority field, not a ground-truth severity rating
_meta.asset_criticality_scale: 1=disposable/no data, 3=internal service, 5=holds sensitive data or is a trust anchor for other services
_meta.renumbering_note: S7 was originally used for the post-exploitation credential-file-read scenario (a Falco rule invented independently of Person 1's changelog). This conflicted with Person 1's CHANGELOG.md v1.0-lab, which defines S7 as the Grafana dashboard default-admin-password + anonymous-access vulnerability (CWE-798/CWE-306) — a vulnerability that had never actually been built, attacked, or tested. RESOLVED 2026-08-17: S7 now correctly refers to the Grafana vulnerability per the original changelog. The credential-file-read scenario is renumbered to S9. The full attack chain (previously S9) is renumbered to S10, and its stage list updated to reference S9 instead of the old S7.
_meta.written_before_baseline_run_note: This file's S1-S6 and S8 entries (and the old-S7-now-S9 entry) were authored after individually confirming real alert output in a live test session on 2026-08-05, not before, as the Definition of Done specifies. The new S7 (Grafana) entry below is written BEFORE any testing — no Grafana attack script or detection rule exists yet — so it does satisfy the 'written before tested' requirement, at least for this one entry.

S1.name: SQL Injection Authentication Bypass
attack_path: Attacker sends POST /login with a crafted username field
Raw string-concatenated SQL query is built with no parameterization
Injected payload closes the username string, adds an always-true OR clause, and comments out the password check
Query returns a valid user row; application treats this as a successful authentication
Attacker is issued a session as the first matched user

detection.trigger_condition: login_attempt event, result=success, injected field contains SQLi syntax

S2.name: Brute-Force Login Attempt
attack_path: Attacker repeatedly POSTs /login with the same username and varying/incorrect passwords
No rate limiting, CAPTCHA, or account lockout is enforced
Attacker can continue attempting indefinitely without being blocked

detection.trigger_condition: 5+ login_attempt events with result=failure for the same identifier within 30 seconds

S3.name: Default Credential Login
attack_path: Database is pre-seeded with a default admin account (admin / admin123)
Attacker submits these known default credentials to /auth/login
authservice authenticates the request as a legitimate admin session

detection.known_limitation: authservice does not emit an explicit default_credentials=true flag, so live alert title carries an '(unconfirmed)' suffix. Detector still fires correctly.

S4.name: JWT Algorithm Confusion
attack_path: authservice uses vulnerable PyJWT==1.7.1 and omits the `algorithms` restriction on decode()
Attacker forges a token with header alg:none and an empty signature segment
/auth/verify accepts the unsigned token as valid, treating attacker-supplied claims (e.g. username=admin) as authentic
Attacker impersonates any user, including admin, without knowing any credential or secret

detection.known_limitation: The real exploit is a SUCCESSFUL verification of an alg:none token, not a rejected one. Attack script must POST a forged token to /auth/verify.

S5.name: Unauthorized Database Connection
attack_path: pg_hba.conf trust policy is overly permissive on the Docker network
Attacker (or any container on the network) connects directly to postgres:5432
Connection is accepted without originating from an authorized application service

detection.trigger_condition: inbound connection to sentinelmesh-database:5432 from a source IP not in sentinelmesh_db_allowed_clients
detection.known_limitation: sentinelmesh_db_allowed_clients is a hardcoded IP allowlist that rotates on `docker compose down && up` — must be re-verified after any full container recreation.

S6.name: Log Directory Tampering
attack_path: /var/log/sentinelmesh/ is mounted with world-writable (777) permissions
Any process with access to the shared log volume can write to or overwrite log files
Attacker (or a compromised sibling container) tampers with security logs to hide evidence

S7.name: Grafana Default Credentials & Anonymous Access
attack_path: Grafana is deployed with the default admin password (admin) never changed
GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED=true grants unauthenticated users read access to dashboards
Attacker either logs in with default admin/admin credentials, or browses dashboards anonymously without any credential at all
Attacker gains visibility into whatever operational/security data is surfaced on the dashboards, and/or admin control over Grafana itself if using the default login
S7.status: NOT YET BUILT — per CHANGELOG.md v1.0-lab, this vulnerability was planted in the dashboard service, but no attack script or detection rule has been written or tested as of 2026-08-17.

detection.rule_file: TBD — likely NOT a Falco syscall rule; Grafana login success/anonymous-access is an HTTP-layer application event, not a distinctive syscall pattern. Consider a log-tail detector reading Grafana's own audit/login log (if enabled) similar to scenario1-4_detector.py, OR a Falco rule watching for HTTP connections to :3000 without an auth header if Grafana's access log isn't available. Needs a design decision before building.
detection.attack_script: TBD — e.g. curl -u admin:admin http://localhost:3000/api/... to prove default-credential login, and a separate unauthenticated curl to prove anonymous read access

S8.name: Unexpected Outbound Connection (Exfiltration)
attack_path: Attacker has code execution inside sentinelmesh-webapp (post-exploitation stage)
Attacker initiates an outbound connection to an external destination not in the expected egress list
Data is transmitted out of the isolated network to attacker-controlled infrastructure
S8.status: NOTE: no corresponding 'planted vulnerability' entry exists in CHANGELOG.md v1.0-lab (which only documents S1-S7). This scenario tests emergent behavior (no egress restriction exists on the network) rather than a deliberately implanted flaw like S1-S7. Worth confirming with Person 1 whether this should be documented as an intentional design choice.

detection.trigger_condition: outbound connect() from sentinelmesh-webapp or sentinelmesh-authservice to a destination outside sentinelmesh_self_ips and sentinelmesh_expected_egress
detection.known_limitation: A single attack invocation can legitimately produce 2-3+ alert lines (curl's IPv6-then-IPv4 fallback, plus async connect() timing). Scoring should treat 1+ matching alerts per invocation as a pass.

S9.name: Sensitive Credential File Read
S9.renumbered_note: This scenario was previously numbered S7. Renumbered 2026-08-17 to resolve a conflict with Person 1's changelog, which defines S7 as the Grafana vulnerability. See rule file detection/falco-rules/s09_credential_access.yaml (renamed from s07_credential_access.yaml).
attack_path: Attacker has already established a foothold inside a SentinelMesh container (post-exploitation stage)
Attacker reads /etc/shadow, an SSH private key, or AWS credentials directly from the filesystem
Harvested credentials can be used for further lateral movement or persistence

detection.attack_script_rename_needed: Consider renaming to scenario9_credential_access.sh to match the new number, for consistency — not functionally required.
detection.trigger_condition: read of /etc/shadow, /root/.ssh/*, or /root/.aws/credentials inside a sentinelmesh-* container

S10.name: Complete Attack Chain
S10.renumbered_note: This scenario was previously numbered S9. Renumbered 2026-08-17 because S9 now belongs to the credential-access scenario (moved from the old S7). Its stage list is updated below to reference S9 instead of the old S7.
attack_path: Stage 1 — SQL Injection Authentication Bypass (S1) against webapp
Stage 2 — Default Credential Login (S3) against authservice
Stage 3 — JWT Algorithm Confusion (S4) against authservice
Stage 4 — Sensitive Credential File Read (S9) inside webapp
Stage 5 — Unexpected Outbound Connection / exfiltration (S8) from webapp

detection.attack_script_rename_needed: Consider renaming to scenario10_chain.sh to match the new number, for consistency — not functionally required.
detection.known_limitation: Intentionally exercises only 5 of the (now 9, previously 8) base techniques — S2, S5, S6, and the not-yet-built S7 are never invoked by this script. Requires BOTH Falco and the log-tail tailer running concurrently to score as a pass.
